response.title: A Machine Learning Framework for Stock Selection
response.label_definition: Rank stocks by return-to-volatility ratio; label the top Q percent as positive and the bottom Q percent as negative; discard middle-ranked stocks. Exact Q and return/volatility lookahead window are unknown from the supplied context.
data_requirements: Chinese stock data for constructing labeled stock instances
Training dataset constructed from Chinese stock data ranging from 2012.08.08 to 2013.02.01
Testing dataset constructed from Chinese stock data ranging from 2013.02.04 to 2013.03.08
244 technical and fundamental features for each stock
model_families: stacking ensemble with DNN and Random Forest base-level classifiers and Logistic Regression meta-level classifier
response.training_protocol: For the selected Stacking model before GA feature selection: use the original training dataset from 2012.08.08 to 2013.02.01 and partition it into three disjoint sets: Train-1, Train-2, and Validation. Train the DNN base classifier on the concatenation of Train-1 and Train-2. Train the RF base classifier solely on Train-2. Train the meta-level Logistic Regression on Validation using predictions from the trained DNN and trained RF as inputs. DNN training uses SGD with Nesterov momentum and learning rate decay and generally converges after 20 epochs; exact batch size, random seed, validation split ratios, DNN architecture details, and loss details are unknown from the supplied context.
response.evaluation_protocol: Fixed chronological holdout statistical evaluation: train on Chinese stock data ranging from 2012.08.08 to 2013.02.01 and test on Chinese stock data ranging from 2013.02.04 to 2013.03.08. The selected result row is the Stacking model before GA feature selection.

evidence_spans.quote: A Machine Learning Framework for Stock Selection
The essence of stock selection is to distinguish the “good” stocks from the “bad” stocks, which lies into the scenario of classiﬁcation problem.
This paper demonstrates how to apply machine learning algorithms to distinguish “good” stocks from the “bad” stocks.
The effectiveness of the stock selection strategy is validated in Chinese stock market in both statistical and practical aspects
The training dataset is constructed from Chinese stock data ranging from 2012.08.08 to 2013.02.01 and the testing dataset is constructed from 2013.02.04 to 2013.03.08.

In this work, RF and DNN are used as based-level classiﬁers and LR is selected as meta-level algorithm.

We ﬁrst partition the original training dataset into three disjoint sets, named as Train-1, Train-2, and Validation. Train-1 and Train-2 serve as the training set of based-level classiﬁers, in which the DNN is trained on the concatenation of Train-1 and Train-2 and RF is trained solely on Train-2.
Validation is then used to train the meta-level LR model, where the inputs to LR is the predictions from trained-DNN and trained-RF on the Validation.
